books.section: A. The Ascendancy of the New Right

stem: Barron's describes three wings of the conservative movement: Cold War conservatives, pro-business economic conservatives, and the religious and cultural wing. Which of the following best explains how Reagan held all three wings together?

options.text: He paired a military buildup and anti-Communist rhetoric with tax cuts, deregulation, and appeals to traditional values
He promised each wing its top goal and delivered all three fully in his first year in office
options.misconception: Reagan delivered only part of each wing's agenda, and slowly — for example, no constitutional amendment on abortion ever passed.

options.text: He dropped the religious wing's social issues in order to keep business conservatives loyal
options.misconception: Reagan kept voicing social conservatism, and the religious right stayed central to his coalition.

options.text: He united the wings by expanding the federal welfare state that all three opposed
options.misconception: Expanding the welfare state was the opposite of what all three wings wanted.

rationales.A: Background: the military buildup spoke to Cold War conservatives, tax cuts and deregulation to business conservatives, and traditional-values appeals to the religious wing — one program with something for each.
rationales.B: Background: Reagan delivered only part of each wing's agenda, and slowly — for example, no constitutional amendment on abortion ever passed.
rationales.C: Background: Reagan kept voicing social conservatism, and the religious right stayed central to his coalition.
rationales.D: Background: expanding the welfare state was the opposite of what all three wings wanted.
rationales.general:
1. Picture the coalition as three crowds that rarely agreed with one another.
2. Background: Cold War conservatives wanted a harder line abroad, business conservatives wanted lower taxes, and the religious wing wanted traditional values defended.
3. Background: Reagan gave each crowd its headline — the buildup, the tax cuts, and the values language — without forcing them to agree on the rest.
4. He did not deliver everything at once, drop the social issues, or expand welfare.
Remember: Reagan's gift was one program with a prize for each wing.
